## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to implement tenant-scoped policy with real tooling in CNF gateways, focusing on dynamic updates and observability.

## Key Concepts
- OPA integration and Rego scoped by namespace and header
- Dynamic policy updates from ConfigMaps
- Tenant isolation and path/method authorization
- Auditing/observability of authorization decisions via Loki
- Minimal Kubernetes manifests to validate end-to-end

## Code Example
```rego
package cnf.authz

default allow = false

# tenant context comes from header and namespace
allow {
  input.headers["X-TENANT-ID"] == input.namespace
  input.method == "GET"
  startswith(input.path, "/v1/orders")
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle versioned APIs and token-based tenants?
- How would you test policy reloads with zero-downtime rollouts?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical policy design and enforcement in a real multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on OSS Gatekeeper usage, per-namespace configuration, and testability.

Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy referencing namespace ConfigMap values
- Per-tenant overrides via Namespace annotations/config
- Lightweight tests to verify enforcement
- Minimal YAML scaffolding for quick rollout checks

Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: defines RateLimitTemplate for K8sRateLimit
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sratelimittemplate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRateLimit
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sratelimit
      # Pseudocode: reads per-namespace cnf.rate-limit and enforces a per-minute cap
      defaultRate := 100
      rateLimitPerMin := data.rateLimitPerMin
      # implementation would map namespace to rate and count requests
      # returns deny if burst exceeds rate
```

```yaml
# Constraint: per-tenant rate limit value
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sRateLimit
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rate-limit
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      kinds: ["Namespace"]
  parameters:
    rateLimitPerMin: 200
    targetPath: "/gateway"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest overriding default rate for tenant-a
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    cnf.rate-limit: "200"  # override default 100/min
```

```yaml

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:

  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: curl

    command: ["sh", "-c", "for i in {1..150}; do curl -s http://gateway-service/gateway || true; done"]
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses real-world upgrade discipline in cloud-native networking functions (CNF): zero-downtime deployments, per-tenant TLS key rotation, and reliable KMS-backed certificate flows—all in a multi-tenant Kubernetes environment.

## Key Concepts
- Canary rollouts with per-namespace traffic control using progressive traffic shifting
- CSR-based TLS rotation via an in-cluster KMS-backed Certificate Authority
- TenantRotation CRD to trigger cross-namespace certificate refresh
- Readiness probes with TLS handshake validation during upgrades
- Traffic shadows for testing new versions without affecting production

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        version: v1.y
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
        - name: KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
          value: "kubernetes.default.svc"
        - name: VAULT_ADDR
          value: "http://vault-in-cluster:8200"
```

```yaml
# Example 2: TenantRotation CRD for per-tenant TLS rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-mtls-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: tenant-a-mtls-secret
  duration: 24h
  renewBefore: 12h
  issuerRef:
    name: kms-tenant-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
  commonName: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: security.example.com/v1
kind: TenantRotation
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rotation
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenantNamespace: tenant-a
  certificateRef:
    name: tenant-mtls-cert
  rotationStrategy: rolling
  preRotationValidation:
    enabled: true
    timeout: 30s
```

```yaml
# Example 3: Minimal one-namespace test manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-tenant
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-ca-key
  namespace: test-tenant
type: Opaque
data:
  ca.key: <base64-encoded-key>
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: test-ca-issuer
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: test-ca-key
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway-test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        env:
        - name: TENANT_NAMESPACE
          value: test-tenant
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  selector:
    app: gateway-test
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8443
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests ability to implement zero-downtime upgrades in a multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on per-tenant isolation, cross-namespace coordination, and robust failure handling.

## Key Concepts
- Graceful drain: per-tenant drain window, preStop, readiness gates
- Global upgrade control: ConfigMap flag
- Control-plane signaling: endpoint or event
- Failure modes: stuck drains, failed signal, burst load

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-upgrade
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  upgradePause: "true"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway-tenant-a
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: cnf/gateway:latest
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9000/drain || true"]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 9000
              protocol: HTTP
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 5
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the drain behavior under bursty traffic?
- How would you handle tenants with long-lived streams (WebSockets)?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement tenant-scoped feature gating, combining CRDs, policy-as-code, and canary-style risk mitigation in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- FeatureGate CRD and TenantFeatureGate per-tenant
- OPA Gatekeeper: ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Path-based canary gating and per-tenant isolation
- Minimal YAML for CRD, policy, namespace, and a basic test

## Code Example
```yaml
# FeatureGate CRD (simplified)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featuregates.example.org
spec:
  group: example.org
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featuregates
    singular: featuregate
    kind: FeatureGate
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (OPA)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sfeaturegate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sFeatureGate
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sfeaturegate
        violation["deny"] {
          input.target.path == "/v1/beta"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["tenant/feature-v1-beta"] == "enabled"
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-tenant)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sFeatureGate
metadata:
  name: tenant-v1beta-enabled
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["gateway.example.org"]
        kinds: ["GatewayRoute"]
  parameters:
    # feature flag key used in tenant annotation
    flagKey: "tenant/feature-v1-beta"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest enabling the flag
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    tenant/feature-v1-beta: enabled
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Revocation through CRLs and transparency logs
- Offline edge verification with bundled certificates
- Minimal scheduling impact through async verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example Kyverno policy for CNF provenance enforcement
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: cnf-provenance-policy
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-image-signature
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
    verifyImages:
    - imageReferences:
      - "*"
      required: true
      attestors:
      - entries:
        - keys:
            kms: "aws-kms://key-id"
      attestations:
      - predicateType: "spdx"
        conditions:
        - all:
          - key: "{{ attestor.metadata.name }}"
            operator: Equals
            value: "tenant-{{ request.namespace }}"
```
